paras: The Texas, Maryland, dynamite explosions were two blasts set off by unknown persons near the village of Texas, on the "N. C. R. R.," on the night of 5-6 May 1903, one of them at the house of a Black man, Arch Wye. Damage was slight and no one was reported hurt, but the local paper said the blasts were rumored to be aimed at intimidating Black and foreign laborers who had come to work at the area's quarries.

Texas was a village with quarries and lime kilns, among them the Bosley lime kilns. According to the Baltimore County Union, "exception is taken to the colored and some foreign laborers coming to work about the quarries."

The first explosion came about 8:30 on Tuesday evening at a stone house occupied by Arch Wye, described as "colored," where dynamite had been placed at the sill of one of the doors. The building shook and its occupants were "greatly alarmed." About 2 o'clock the next morning a second charge went off near the Bosley lime kilns, where men were tending the kilns and were "greatly excited." Both reports were heard a considerable distance from the village, and damage at each place was slight.
The paper described the perpetrators only as "some person or persons unknown" and noted "considerable anxiety among residents." No report of an arrest or investigation appears in the coverage.

The only known account is a brief local item in the Baltimore County Union of Towsontown, published on 9 May 1903 under the heading "Dynamite Explosions Cause Alarm." The item framed the episode around residents' alarm and gave the motive only as hearsay ("It is said"), without comment on the intimidation of the laborers. No other white paper and no Black paper is known to have reported the explosions.
